Curious as to what other people read and enjoyed anywhere from grade 8-12. I especially welcome anyone raised outside of Canada/US to share! There are surely hundreds of great European English and non-English works being taught around the world that aren't often mentioned this side of the internet.

I remember really enjoying The Last Book in The Universe, The Giver, and Maus I & II. From what I can remember of my least favourites, I found The Great Gatsby to be pretty boring at the time. Also--admitting this always makes me feel like some sort of heathen?--I loathed reading Shakespeare. And there was always Shakespeare. (Though, in hindsight, it might of had more to do with teaching style rather than the actual content.)
Favourite/least favourite books from your school days?

Animal farm. Don't get me wrong . I hate it in the beginning because I was forced to read it. But I liked the characters, and the story . I didn't get the message of the book until I reread it last year
Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde. I mean don't get me wrong, it's a great book and I came to appreciate it later on. But when I was introduced to it in class, I just didn't like it.

I remember being forced to read Across Five Aprils really young, and I still have trouble with historical fiction from how much I hated to read that novel. On the flip side, I really enjoyed Fahrenheit 451, and Shakespeare I really enjoyed for some reason. Maybe it was the dick jokes.

Favorite (possibly of all time) is Flowers for Algernon, the more often I read it the earlier in the book I start crying. My least favorite was probably Moby Dick, I didn't feel like I learned nearly enough about whaling to make it worth it.

Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness, truly one of the best books I've ever read. It had this boyish adventurous feel while also delving deep into the psychology of racism both explicitly and on a meta-level. We read it alongside Achebe's Things Fall Apart.

Favorite books from school: shabanu daughter of the wind, summer by Edith Wharton, great expectations,the red pony, the great Gatsby, & Ivanhoe. My friends used to call me wamba daughter of witless. I have never been able to by past the first couple of pages of Moby dick. Also the old man and the sea is the shortest most boring book I've ever read in my life.
I loved reading The Odyssey and Beowulf in high school. They got me on a myth/legend reading binge, where I went on to read other stories such as Egil's Saga.

Absolute favorites:

  • Catch-22
  • The Great Gatsby
  • One Flew Over The Cuckoo's Nest
  • The Things They Carried
  • The Awakening

Least:

  • Their Eyes Were Watching God

My least favourite of the books I had to read in school is either Enduring Love or Anthem.

I don't think I'll ever forget the day I asked /lit/ "I hate Anthem, but as famous as Ayn Rand is she had to be doing something right. What book can I read to get her at her best?". The first reply said "I cannot in good conscience recommend any Ayn Rand book."

From elementary school, I remember The Cay by Theodore Taylor and Underground to Canada by Barbara Smucker. Good reads. Also Deirdre Kessler the Brupp series.

In junior high, the memorable books were The Red Pony by John Steinbeck, Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of NIMH by Robert C O'Brien and The Cremation of Sam McGee by Robert W Service.

In high school I was introduced to Thomas Hardy, more Steinbeck, Harper Lee and more classical literature. I loved it, but many people didn't :) The teachers typically kept their reading lists public, so they introduced us to people like Clive Cussler and Suzanne Collins and encouraged reading for fun.

In 10th grade I had a teacher who personally assigned me to read Ishmael by Daniel Quinn. At 16, that book made quite an impression on me. It was a book I digested in two sittings and thought about for years afterwords.

I loved pretty much everything I had to read. I really liked the short story Harrison Bergeron I had to read in 7th grade. I enjoyed Crime and Punishment and East of Eden even though my classmates didn't. (I enjoy most of the classics and Shakespeare we read.) I really did not enjoy Their Eyes Were Watching God or The Joy Luck Club.

Least: Tale of Two Cities. Dickens. A lot of British literature from the 19th century and previous, excepting Shakespeare, if I'm being honest. Dull fucking writing and bad fucking writing abound. I eventually learned to appreciate Two Cities a bit more in college, because the professor was honest about it being very far from a timeless work. Liked Gatsby, didn't hate Catcher, quite enjoyed Huck Finn, had read 451 previously at a more appropriate age (like... nine, maybe) - I think that covers the other usual suspects.

Favorite: really liked The Things They Carried. I was at an age when the idea of varying types of truth was novel to me, and entertaining. Plus, that book at least told you it wasn't based in events that had really happened, unlike most of the narrative-before-fact stuff you see nowadays. And it was always fun to read an assigned book that espoused the fuckin' fuckity fuckword back in high school.

Before that, back in middle school, I feel like mentioning that the whole world seemed to be on a YA Oprah-style novel kick, which I thought was revolting. "Realistic fiction" - fucking garbage. All a bunch of watered-down morality stories about growing up in the ghetto and making good decisions while the older brother falls into gang violence. Because that was something to which we white, suburbanite tweens could relate. Clearly. It was inevitably inane, and I hope that trend has died off.

Hello all! I recently became interested in multicopters and would like to start with a budget 250mm quadcopter build to get into the hobby. I've been watching a lot of videos and reading articles to develop a base of knowledge, but I figure I'd tap into people's experiences here before I order any bits.

So, I'm looking for a "best bang for buck" 250mm quadcopter that I can build myself. I can solder, but I have zero experience with models or RC. I have no kit at all, so I would be starting from scratch. I'd like to know which components you would recommend to a novice to get this thing off the ground! Thanks!

If it helps, I'm in Canada.

Buy a hubsan x4 or a blade nano or a cheerson and learn to fly. Then one of your best bangs for the buck is myrcmart - $$$ for shipping but they have everything you could want at decent prices. They have 250 kits for a good price, and you can always build a quad FPV ready then add FPV gear later. But definitely learn to fly first or you'll spend a lot more money in repairs.
